_note: How a long-form video's runtime actually breaks down. Auto-generated transcripts were cut into ~30-second blocks and each block scored for how its time divides between the presenter's own substance, source material read aloud, filler, and promotion. A one-off study, not a live feed.
_method: The 12 most recent long-form uploads on TheQuartering that have transcripts, as of 2026-08-07 — 333 blocks covering 171 minutes. Every block was scored twice, independently, by two different models, each shown the neighbouring blocks for context. Rather than forcing one label per block, each rater split the block's time across the four categories, so a block that is half quotation and half his own point counts as half of each. The two agreed on 73% of blocks; the 89 where they materially disagreed were settled by a third pass with a wider window of transcript. Blocks are weighted by their real duration.
_caveat: Substance vs read-aloud is the softest line, because auto-transcripts carry no quotation marks. Where a rater was genuinely torn the rules told it to favour substance over filler, so the filler figure is a floor rather than a ceiling. The combined 'not filler, not promo' share is the firmer number.
